crossrefs.text: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
If a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to obligate himself by a pledge, he must not break his word; he must do everything he has promised.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.
Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe.
“For our God is a consuming fire.”
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for oneʼs life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.

There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
I saw that all labor and success spring from a manʼs envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
Place no trust in extortion, or false hope in stolen goods. If your riches increase, do not set your heart upon them.
“Look at the man who did not make God his refuge, but trusted in the abundance of his wealth and strengthened himself by destruction.”
saying: “Naked I came from my motherʼs womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
For when he dies, he will carry nothing away; his abundance will not follow him down.
There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.
On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.

So Lot went out and spoke to the sons-in-law who were pledged in marriage to his daughters. “Get up,” he said. “Get out of this place, for the Lordis about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
But remember that it is the LORD your God who gives you the power to gain wealth, in order to confirm His covenant that He swore to your fathers even to this day.
and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
therefore wisdom and knowledge have been granted to you. And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.”
I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,
and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?

God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
